html: Lipi, or Lípez, is the name of an Indigenous people and region in the far south-west of Bolivia, on the high altiplano around the Uyuni salt flat and the borders of Chile and Argentina. Its people herded llamas, hunted vicuña, gathered salt and traded across the desert toward the Atacama; they are often linked to the Atacameño and Uru peoples. The region came under the Inca and then the Spanish, whose silver mines at Potosí, the source of Potosí silver, lay to the north-east. The provinces of Nor Lípez and Sud Lípez keep the name.
